children.text: TL;DR:

The gap between what gets said in a meeting and what ends up in the notes is where decisions go wrong. Most meeting note tools produce summaries that describe topics rather than capture specifics: You get "discussed pricing" instead of the actual number, "agreed to follow up" instead of who committed to what by when. Granola is an AI notepad built to close that gap. You jot rough notes during the meeting. Granola enhances them with specific quotes, figures, and context drawn from the full transcript. Cross-meeting intelligence lets you query patterns across your full archive with source-linked citations. If audio playback or automated conversation analytics are your primary need, Granola is not the right fit: it transcribes and enhances your notes rather than keeping audio for playback. If accurate, retrievable, human-guided notes are what you need, setup takes under five minutes. Free to start.

Back-to-back meetings create a documentation gap. You are either fully present or taking detailed notes, rarely both. The cost of that gap is concrete: decisions made from vague summaries, action items without owners, commitments that never make it into the record. The tools you choose to bridge that gap affect the quality of what gets captured.

The best AI for summarizing meeting notes is not the one that captures the most raw text. It is the one that produces notes specific enough to act on: the right figures, the right commitments, attributed to the right people. Human judgment has to stay in the loop, because the details worth capturing are the ones you recognized as important in the room.
What makes meeting note summarization effective in high-stakes environments
Granola is built around three principles for high-stakes meeting environments:
Capture architecture:

Granola transcribes from device audio and works across Zoom, Google Meet, Slack huddles and in-person conversations picked up by your laptop, so the same workflow applies wherever the meeting happens.
Summary fidelity:

Granola preserves specific metrics by using your rough notes as a guide. You write what matters, Granola fills in details from the transcript, avoiding generic summaries like "founder discussed market opportunity."
Cross-meeting intelligence:

Granola lets you query patterns across any collection of meetings. Ask a question and get a cited answer drawn from every relevant conversation. Each conversation becomes part of a searchable knowledge base rather than an isolated event.
How Granola achieves summary accuracy

Accuracy here means semantic precision, not word-for-word transcription. A summary that outputs "the founder discussed market opportunity and competitive landscape" is technically accurate and completely useless. What you need are the specific figures and claims: The actual ARR number, the growth rate, the conversion metric, not a description of the topic.
The critical variable is how the input is structured. Fully automated tools take everything said and produce a generic output.
Granola's AI-enhanced notes

use your rough notes as a compass: If you jot "market sizing claim," the AI searches the full transcript and surfaces every relevant exchange, including specific figures and quotes. Leave the notepad blank and the output reverts to a generic summary. Write specific notes and the output reflects your actual priorities.
Validating your meeting note accuracy
Participants cite specific figures: a customer's churn rate, a candidate's timeline, a prospect's budget. Those details need to survive the trip to the written record.

Granola keeps your original notes in black and places AI-enhanced details in gray. That visual separation lets you immediately identify what you wrote versus what the AI added from the transcript. You approve, edit, or delete each addition before it becomes part of the permanent record, so no AI-generated detail slips into a memo unreviewed.

Granola: Built for meetings where the details matter

Granola is an AI notepad built for professionals in back-to-back meetings, from sales calls and customer interviews to board sessions and founder pitches. Review the gray additions, edit or delete anything that misses the mark, and export a structured note that reflects your priorities, not a generic summary of everything said.

children.text: Verifying AI action item extraction

Generic action item extraction produces outputs like "founder to follow up" or "team to schedule next call." Those are useless without an owner, a specific commitment, and a timeframe. High-precision extraction captures the specific owner, commitment, and timeframe, not just a category label like "team to follow up."
Granola's enhanced notes highlight action items in gray for your approval. You see the specific commitment and timeframe. Review each action item before it becomes part of the permanent record. The

How note quality shapes professional conversations

Granola keeps your attention on the conversation rather than on writing everything down, and fills in the specifics from the transcript afterwards: the figures a customer cited, the timeline a candidate gave, the commitment a founder made. Users report that the notes they end up with are more specific than what they could have typed live.

For investment conversations, the value of a note is in its specifics. Granola pulls the ARR figure, the growth rate and the named commitment out of the transcript and places them under the bullets you wrote, so the memo you draft afterwards rests on what was actually said.
Capturing detail across meeting types

Granola transcribes from device audio, so the same workflow applies whether you are running a customer research session, a recruiting interview, or a founder pitch. It works across Zoom, Google Meet, Slack huddles, and in-person conversations picked up by your laptop microphone.
Matching meeting types to AI summarization depth

Different meetings produce different kinds of decisions, and the documentation depth should match. A standup produces action items. A discovery call produces objections and next steps. A pitch conversation produces claims, metrics, and commitments that feed a structured memo. In each case, the note has to be specific enough to act on when the meeting is over.

You can ask "What did the founder say about enterprise sales motion across our three conversations?" and get a cited answer that pulls from all three meeting notes.

FAQs
How do you measure AI summarizer fidelity?

A high-fidelity summarizer captures exact figures: The specific ARR number, the growth rate, the named customer, rather than vague generalizations like "discussed revenue." It attributes claims to the correct speaker without combining context from different conversation segments.
How precise is AI at logging action items?

Precision is measured by whether the AI assigns a specific owner and timeframe to each task, not just a generic label. Granola extracts action items directly from the transcript, with owner and timeframe, and highlights them in gray so you can verify, edit, or delete each one before it enters the permanent record. This applies regardless of meeting type: the specific commitment and timeframe are captured, not a category label.
How does Granola handle meeting privacy?

Choose a tool with a privacy-first architecture. Granola is SOC 2 Type 2 certified (July 2025), deletes audio immediately after transcription, and contractually prohibits third-party AI models from training on your meeting data. For participants, Granola includes built-in tools to keep people informed, including an automated chat message posted in your meeting chat when transcription starts, and a video watermark that makes transcription visible without requiring a bot to join the call.
How long does it take to get AI meeting reports?
Granola captures device audio and transcribes in real time, so notes are enhanced in seconds the moment you click "Enhance."
Glossary
Bot-free capture:

A transcription method in which no named participant joins the meeting call. The app captures audio from the device's microphone and speakers directly, so no visible third-party participant appears in the attendee list.
Device audio:
The audio output from your computer's speakers and microphone.
Enhanced notes:

The output Granola produces after a meeting ends. You write rough notes during the call. Granola searches the full transcript and adds specific quotes, figures, and context in gray beneath each bullet. You review, edit, or delete each addition before it enters the permanent record.
Cross-meeting intelligence:

The ability to query across your full archive of meeting notes rather than searching one conversation at a time. Granola's chat returns source-linked citations drawn from every relevant meeting, so patterns across dozens of conversations surface in a single answer.
Recipes:

Saved prompt templates in Granola that extract a specific output from any meeting note with a single click. Built-in examples include daily briefings via /Prep my day and follow-up email formats. You can also build custom Recipes for recurring meeting formats, such as a structured memo draft from a pitch note. Recipes are shareable across a team and accessible from the Recipes library.
